name: Locality-preserving Densification
definition: A densification strategy addressing the throttling factor of memory layout, where adding new Gaussians at the end of parameter buffers causes spatially close Gaussians to be far apart in memory, resulting in uncoalesced memory accesses.
summary: Locality-preserving Densification reorders Gaussian buffers using Z-ordering to ensure spatially close primitives are adjacent in memory, improving hardware efficiency rather than geometric splitting criteria.
